items.title: Section: Gathering the Whole Mind, and Seeking to Hear the Teaching Concludes

items.zh: 五者、攝一切心聽聞正法。
items.en: Fifth, hearing the true teaching with the whole mind gathered in. ... Holding the mind entirely in mindfulness at every moment is for the sake of understanding, without gap, the sound, wording, and phrasing and their meaning — so that nothing goes unknown, nothing goes unpenetrated, and the time spent passes not in vain.

items.zh: 菩薩如是求聞正法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas in this way seek to hear the true teaching.

items.title: Section: Why Seek the Teaching? Purposes Named for Inner Teaching and for Logic

items.zh: 菩薩何故求聞正法？謂諸菩薩求內明時，為正修行法隨法行，為廣開示利悟於他。
items.en: Why do bodhisattvas seek to hear the true teaching? Bodhisattvas, in seeking inner teaching, do so in order to practise correctly in accordance with the dharma, and in order to broadly explain it so as to benefit and awaken others.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩求因明時，為欲如實了知外道所造因論是惡言說；為欲降伏他諸異論；為欲於此真實聖教，未淨信者令其淨信，已淨信者倍令增廣。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in seeking logic, do so in order to truly recognise that the causal theories devised by other schools are flawed reasoning; in order to subdue various rival doctrines; and in order that, towards this genuine noble teaching, those without pure faith may come to have it, and those who already have pure faith may have it doubled and expanded.

items.title: Why Seek Grammar, Medicine, and the Practical Arts

items.zh: 若諸菩薩求聲明時，為令信樂典語眾生，於菩薩身深生敬信。為欲悟入詁訓言音文句差別，於一義中種種品類殊音隨說。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in seeking grammar, do so so that beings who trust and delight in refined, well-attested language give rise to deep respect and confidence towards the bodhisattva; and so as to enter into the distinctions of glosses on ancient and dialect words, of sound, and of phrasing, and to freely express, within any one domain of meaning, its many varied kinds of distinct wording.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩求醫明時，為息眾生種種疾病，為欲饒益一切大眾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in seeking medicine, do so in order to bring an end to beings' various illnesses, and in order to benefit the whole community.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩求諸世間工業智處，為少功力多集珍財，為欲利益諸眾生故，為發眾生甚希奇想，為以巧智平等分布，饒益攝受無量眾生。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in seeking worldly practical wisdom and craft, do so in order to gather precious wealth with little effort, in order to benefit beings, in order to give rise to a sense of great wonder in beings, and in order to distribute wisely and impartially through skilful means, benefiting and gathering in countless beings.

items.title: Section: Seeking the Teaching Concludes — What, How, and Why All Now Answered

items.zh: 菩薩求此一切五明，為令無上正等菩提大智資糧速得圓滿。非不於此一切明處次第修學，能得無障一切智智。
items.en: Bodhisattvas seek all five of these fields of knowledge so that the great provisions of wisdom for unsurpassed, perfect awakening may swiftly reach completion. It is not the case that, without training in due order through all these fields of knowledge, one can attain the unobstructed knowledge of all things.

items.zh: 如是已說一切菩薩正所應求，如是而求，為此義求。
items.en: This concludes explaining what all bodhisattvas genuinely should seek, how they should seek it, and for what purpose they seek it.

items.title: Section: A New Question Opens — How Should a Bodhisattva Teach?

items.zh: 菩薩為他說正法時，當何所說？云何而說？何義故說？謂諸菩薩正所應求，即是所說。為此義求，即為此義而為他說。
items.en: When bodhisattvas teach the true teaching to others, what should be taught? How should it be taught? For what purpose is it taught? Whatever bodhisattvas genuinely should seek is exactly what is taught. ... Whatever purpose the seeking is for is exactly the purpose for which it is taught to others.

items.zh: 依二種相應為他說。一者、依隨順說應為他說；二者、依清淨說應為他說。
items.en: Teaching others should rest on two kinds of manner. First, teaching others resting on accommodating speech; second, teaching others resting on pure speech.

items.zh: 云何依隨順說應為他說？

items.title: Section: Accommodating Speech Begins — Proper Time, Weighty Regard, Right Order, Unstinting Continuity

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩應當安住如法威儀而為他說，非不安住如法威儀。不為無病處高座者而說正法，不為坐者立說正法，不應居後為前行者而說正法，不為覆頭而說正法。如別解脫經廣說應知。何以故？諸佛菩薩敬重法故。
items.en: Bodhisattvas should abide in proper, dharma-fitting posture when teaching others, never teaching without such proper posture. One does not teach true teaching to someone who, though not ill, sits on a high seat; one does not teach standing to someone seated; one does not teach from behind someone walking ahead; one does not teach to someone whose head remains covered. ... Why is this? Because buddhas and bodhisattvas revere the teaching itself.

items.zh: 又於正法生尊重時，令他於法起極珍貴，恭敬聽聞而不輕毀。又為一切說一切法，無間而說。又於正法不生慳悋，不作師拳。
items.en: And when giving rise to reverence for the true teaching, one causes others to regard the teaching as utterly precious, listening respectfully rather than treating it lightly. And one teaches the whole of the teaching to everyone, teaching without interruption. And, towards the true teaching, one gives rise to no stinginess, never acting like a teacher who keeps a closed fist.

items.title: According with the Text, Bringing Real Benefit, and Making the Teaching Welcome

items.zh: 又於正法，如其文句次第而標，如其文句次第而釋，如其次第分別其義。又若引攝義利法義，應標、應釋、應廣分別，非不引攝義利法義。
items.en: And regarding the true teaching, one presents it following the order of its own wording, explains it following the order of its own wording, and distinguishes its meaning following that same order. And whatever teaching draws in genuine benefit should be presented, explained, and broadly distinguished — never teaching in a way that fails to draw in genuine benefit.

items.zh: 又應示現所應示現。又應教導所應教導。又應讚勵所應讚勵。
items.en: And one shows whatever should be shown. And one instructs whomever should be instructed. And one praises and encourages whomever should be praised and encouraged.

items.title: Section: Never Casting Out, Speaking Only by Valid Means, Meeting Every Assembly Where It Is — Fifteen Marks Complete

items.zh: 又應慶慰所應慶慰。又依現、比至教道理而說正法，非不依彼三量道理。又所宣說順往善趣。又所宣說無亂、易入，而不隱密。又所宣說應四聖諦。
items.en: And one praises and comforts whomever should be praised and comforted. And one teaches the true teaching resting on direct perception, inference, and reliable scriptural authority, never teaching apart from these three valid means. And what is taught leads towards the favourable realms. And what is taught is free of confusion, easy to enter, and never hidden away. And what is taught accords with the four noble truths.

items.zh: 又處一切眾說正法時，隨眾所應而為宣說。菩薩依此十五種相，諸隨順說普為利他，應如是說。
items.en: And when teaching the true teaching amid any assembly whatsoever, one teaches according to what that assembly itself calls for. ... Bodhisattvas, resting on these fifteen marks of accommodating speech, universally benefiting others, should teach in just this way.

items.zh: 云何依清淨說應為他說？謂諸菩薩，於己有怨諸有情類，應住慈心，為說正法。於行惡行諸有情類，住利益心，應說正法。於諸有樂有苦、放逸下劣有情，應當安住利益安樂哀愍之心，為說正法。

items.title: Section: Pure Speech Concludes — No Self-Praise, No Hidden Motive, and Teaching Itself Concludes

items.zh: 不以嫉纏增上力故，自讚毀他。以無染心，不希利益恭敬讚頌，為他說法。菩薩依止此五種相，諸清淨說普為利他，應如是說。
items.en: One does not, under the sway of jealousy, praise oneself while disparaging others. ... With a mind free of any taint, not hoping for gain, honour, or praise, one teaches others. ... Bodhisattvas, resting on these five marks, universally benefiting others, should teach in just this way.

items.zh: 如是菩薩說正法相略有二十。一者、以時，二者、重法，三者、次第，四者、相續，五者、隨順，六者、歡喜，七者、愛樂，八者、悅豫，九者、欣勇，十者、不擯，十一者、應理，十二者、稱順，十三者、無亂，十四者、如法，十五者、順眾，十六者、慈心，十七者、利益心，十八者、哀愍心，十九者、不自讚毀他，二十者、不依利養恭敬讚頌。菩薩如是應常為他宣說正法。
items.en: In this way, the marks of a bodhisattva teaching the true teaching are, in brief, twenty in number. ... Bodhisattvas should, in just this way, constantly teach the true teaching to others.

blocks.text: Why a bodhisattva studies each of the five sciences, and how to teach well. The list of twenty marks of good teaching is practical advice for any teacher.

**Inner knowledge**: "to practise correctly, and to explain it widely for others". **Logic**: "to recognise the causal theories of other schools as flawed", and to subdue them. **Linguistics**: so that those "who delight in refined language" respect the bodhisattva. **Medicine**: "to end beings' illnesses". **Crafts**: "to gather wealth with little effort, to benefit beings". "Without training in all five, omniscience cannot be attained."
"What bodhisattvas should seek is exactly what they teach." Teaching rests on **accommodating speech** and **pure speech**.

Proper posture: one does not teach "someone without illness seated on a high seat" while oneself standing. At the right time; with reverence for the teaching; in the right order; "not stingy with the Dharma, making no teacher's fist" (Venerable Miào Jìng: like a martial-arts master who holds back the last move); following the order of the text; showing, instructing, praising, encouraging; "resting on direct perception, inference, and scripture"; and meeting each assembly where it is. Fifteen marks in all.

"One does not, from envy, praise oneself and disparage others." "With a mind free of taint, not hoping for gain, honour, or praise." Venerable Miào Jìng: envy is being unable to bear others' good. Five marks, twenty in all.

quiz.q: Inner teaching is sought "to practise in accordance with the Dharma." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain, citing the Mahāvibhāṣā?
options: 法 is nirvāṇa, 隨法 the eightfold path, 行 practice
quiz.why: "When seeking inner teaching, bodhisattvas do so to practise correctly in accordance with the Dharma, and to open it widely to others." Master Cháng Bǎi: first, the Mahāvibhāṣā says 法 is nirvāṇa; 隨法 the eightfold path; 行 practice.

quiz.q: Seeking logic "to know outsiders' causal theories are ill-spoken." What is their main problem, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: causeless and unequal-cause theories, which logic can counter
quiz.why: "When seeking logic, bodhisattvas do so to truly know that the causal treatises of other paths are ill-spoken." Master Cháng Bǎi: as the Compendium of Topics says, outsiders' theories mainly suffer from causelessness and unequal causes; logic can counter such ill speech.

quiz.q: Seeking linguistics "so that beings who love refined language respect the bodhisattva." What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: refined speech is elegant, not rustic; Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas must know literature — especially Chinese, which preserves the scriptures most completely
quiz.why: "When seeking linguistics, they do so in order that beings who delight in refined language may deeply respect the bodhisattva." Venerable Miào Jìng: refined language means speech that isn't rustic — elegant phrasing. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas must understand literature — Chinese literature above all, since the scriptures are most completely translated in it.

quiz.q: Seeking practical crafts "to gather much wealth with little effort." Who may do so, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: lay bodhisattvas — gathering much wealth with little effort
quiz.why: "When seeking worldly crafts, they do so to gather much wealth with little effort, to benefit beings." Master Cháng Bǎi: lay bodhisattvas can do this — accumulating much precious wealth with little effort.

quiz.q: "Not teaching to one without illness on a high seat" — the English makes the healthy one the teacher. What do the lectures say?
options: both: the healthy one on the high seat is the listener — one doesn't teach a healthy listener seated above
quiz.why: "They do not teach the true Dharma to one without illness seated on a high seat, nor stand while teaching one who is seated." Venerable Miào Jìng: he isn't ill, he's on a high seat, you're on a low seat teaching him — that's not done. Master Cháng Bǎi: not teaching a healthy person seated high, not standing to teach one seated. The English and note make the healthy one the teacher — backwards.

quiz.q: "Not stingy with the Dharma, not making a teacher's fist." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "teacher's fist"?
options: like a martial-arts master keeping one move secret
quiz.why: "They are not stingy with the true Dharma, and make no teacher's fist." Venerable Miào Jìng: say you're learning martial arts, and the teacher keeps this one move secret.

quiz.q: Pure speech: "not praising oneself and disparaging others through envy." How does Venerable Miào Jìng define envy?
options: envy is being unable to bear another's glory
quiz.why: "Not, through the dominating force of envy, praising oneself and disparaging others." Venerable Miào Jìng: envy is being unable to bear another's glory.
